prompt: Ship a tracking plan for our checkout funnel events.
assertions: Produces a tracking-plan table (event/properties/type/owner/status), not just prose advice
Enforces one naming grammar (object-action, one casing, one tense) rather than leaving casing/tense open per event
Reserved properties (revenue/currency/value) are flagged as a contract, not left as free-form fields
States the schema evolution rule per event (e.g. MODEL-REVISION-ADDITION) so a future breaking change has a defined bump

prompt: Write a data contract between the payments service and the analytics warehouse.
assertions: Produces an ODCS-shaped contract (fundamentals/schema/quality/SLA sections), not a free-text description
Schema fields carry pii/classification flags, not just name/type
Data-quality rules are assigned to one of the four ODCS tiers (text/library/sql/custom), not left as vague prose
SLA properties carry a driver (regulatory/analytics/operational), used to justify the SLA value chosen
Notes that ODCS is the current spec (not the deprecated DCS) and flags the version as something to re-verify

prompt: Build the quality gate for our marts layer before the next dbt run ships.
assertions: Covers both known-unknowns (rule tests) and unknown-unknowns (anomaly/statistical detection) — not just one
Every primary key has both unique and not_null as the non-negotiable floor
Assigns checks to a layer (staging vs marts vs all-with-history) per the where-to-run-checks convention, not everything dumped at one layer
Includes a PR-time / pre-merge blast-radius check before checks are declared complete

prompt: Recommend sync strategies for five source tables of different shapes.
assertions: Assigns a strategy per table shape (full_refresh/incremental/append/CDC/webhook), not one strategy for everything
States the reason each table got its strategy, tied to its shape (row count, bookmark column, append-only, latency need)
Flags CDC as snapshot-then-log-tail, not infinite streaming, and calls out the new-table-CDC-lag gotcha
States the at-least-once / resumable-checkpoint invariant rather than assuming a single retry-free read

prompt: Audit our warehouse for PII exposure and fix the gaps before the next access review.
assertions: Follows classify -> tag -> platform-mask -> retention/erasure -> verify as ordered stages, not a single flat list
Masking is enforced at the platform/warehouse layer (tags/policies), not proposed as an application-layer fix
Erasure logic checks GDPR Art.17 exception grounds before deleting — does not default to 'delete everything on request'
Warehouse deletion is specified as tombstone + scheduled hard-delete, not in-place mutation of historical tables
Includes a verification step that actually tests a denied/masked path, not just a design description

prompt: We think our warehouse bill is too high before we've even scaled — sanity-check the architecture.
assertions: Asks workload-shape questions (measured bytes-scanned, predictability, real latency need) before recommending an architecture change
Checks whether the current design was sized against sample/dev data rather than measured production volume
Names auto-suspend and right-sizing as the first levers, before recommending architectural changes
Any $/TiB or $/slot-hour figure cited is date-stamped with an instruction to re-verify against the live pricing page
